notes:
Account snapshot: MapleRow is a mid-market SaaS that powers in-app conversational support and knowledge retrieval for several fintech and health verticals. Started on Redwood Hosted API for rapid feature rollout (Nov 2025). After stable functional tests, they requested a Dedicated option for cost predictability, data isolation, and higher sustained throughput.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-11-12: Intro call (Jordan) - product overview, quick Hosted API trial setup; SE invited.
- 2025-12-03: Hosted API demo (Priya) - 2 sample flows, streaming response test; team liked low latency p50 ~ 80-100ms on hosted for short chats.
- 2026-01-18: POC kick-off (dedicated sizing discussion) - outlined expected baseline qps, KV cache needs, concurrency limits.
- 2026-02-10: POC run 1 (Priya + infra) - sustained throughput test: 35 rps at 95%ile latency 210ms; token cost estimates validated vs hosted.
- 2026-02-15: PoC review (ff_20260215_maplerow_poc_call) - product feedback: "good quality, need 2x headroom for peak promotional bursts".
- 2026-02-25: Legal & security pre-review - asked for SOC2 report, SAML SSO integration guide, and KMS/HSM options.
- 2026-02-28: Pricing workshop (Jordan + finance lead) - discussed commit tiers, burst credits, overage formulas, and ramp mechanics.

Technical / requirements summary:
- Workloads: chat-heavy support assistant + embeddings for doc search + reranking for response selection.
- Throughput targets: baseline 25-40 rps per cluster, with spikes up to 80 rps during campaigns.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms for chat, p95 < 350ms acceptable for heavier multimodal prompts.
- Cost sensitivity: unit cost must be predictable — finance requests committed monthly GPU-hours model vs raw per-token billing.
- Model preferences: open Llama-like finetuned family; Redwood-verified medium-latency profile preferred. Must support quantized variants.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to lower-cost variant during capacity constraints and regional failover (NA primary, EU residency for EU customers).
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), SOC2 is mandatory, audit logging and KMS integration required. Data residency clause needed for EU-customer datasets.

POC / performance notes:
- Hosted API trial was low-friction; dev teams used it for feature parity checks.
- Dedicated POC demonstrated stability but saw 1.8x throughput variance under sustained synthetic load. SE recommends kernel tuning + larger KV cache.
- Cache hit-rate improvements reduced token costs in later runs by ~12%.

Pricing & packaging negotiation specifics:
- Preferred structure: 12-month committed GPU-hours with quarterly ramp windows (25% / 50% / 100%). Finance asked for a 6-month ramp option as well.
- Burst model ask: guaranteed baseline capacity + burst pool (pre-paid credits usable at 2x baseline) with an option to purchase one-off extra GPU-hours at fixed rate.
- Overage discussion: MapleRow requests capped overage (% of committed) per month or an overage multiplier capped at 1.5x of unit price. Legal prefers explicit overage-rate schedule.
- Early termination / ramp down: they want a 60-day notice and pro-rated credits back for long-term commits; Redwood legal to evaluate.
- Metrics for billing: prefer bill-by-GPU-hour + token adjustment factor for small responses; Redwood suggested hybrid token + GPU-hour model — currently under review.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- Head of Product: "We need a contract that lets us scale into peak campaigns without the bill shock."
- Finance lead: "We can accept a ramp but require clear ceilings on overages + predictable effective ARR."
- Platform engineer: "Need VPC & SAML now — also wanting offline model variant for EU customers."

Risks & open items:
- Procurement wants final TCO comparison vs Hosted over 24 months (include expected cache savings).
- Need clarity on burst enforcement (queueing vs immediate capacity spin-up) and expected latency under burst.
- Legal to provide redlines for data residency/retention before SOW signs.
- SE to run repeat POC at 3/50/80 rps sustained to validate tuning recommendations (Priya action).

Next concrete steps (action log):
- 2026-03-05: SE (Priya) to run tuned POC and upload results to Drive (assigned).
- 2026-03-07: Jordan to circulate pricing spreadsheet (3/6/12 month commit options + burst+overage cells) to MapleRow finance. (drive link included).
- 2026-03-10: Legal sync meeting to review MSA redlines (Jordan + Redwood legal + MapleRow counsel).
- Finance approval goal: 2026-03-24 (internal at MapleRow).

- Offer 2 pricing templates: (A) 12-month commit with 3-stage ramp + discounted burst pool, (B) 6-month pilot commit with higher unit price and clear overage cap. Include explicit example invoices in Drive.
- Pre-approve SOC2 + SAML integration docs into the security FAQ and surface KMS options in the SOW.
- SE: complete tuned POC and include cache sizing recommendations to reduce variance.

Status summary: In procurement; pricing negotiations focused on Dedicated commit terms (commit level, burst credits, overage cap, ramp schedule). Target close: March 2026 (subject to legal/finance sign-off).
